item.dc:title: 2Dinsight3D: an multi-modal urban scene dataset for point cloud semantic segmentation from remote sensing imagery
item.dc:creator: Yiping Chen Chenlu Lin Ting Han Weiquan Liu Yu Zang Jonathan Li Cheng Wang a School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University, Zhuhai, Chinab Fujian Key Laboratory of Sensing and Computing for Smart Cities, School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Chinac Key Laboratory of Multimedia Trusted Perception and Efficient Computing, Ministry of Education, School of Informatics, Xiamen University, Xiamen, Chinad College of Computer Engineering, Jimei University, Xiamen, Chinae Department of Geography and Environmental Management, University of Waterloo, Waterloo, CanadaYiping Chen received the Ph.D. degree in information communication engineering from the National University of Defense Technology, in 2011. From 2007 to 2011, she was an Assistant Researcher with The Chinese University of Hong Kong. She is currently a Professor with the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. Her main research interests include image processing, mobile LiDAR data analysis, and GeoAI.Chenlu Lin received the B.S. degree from the Xiamen University, in 2023. He is currently pursuing the M.S. degree with the ASC Laboratory, Xiamen University. His research interests include point cloud representation learning and deep learning.Ting Han is currently pursuing his Ph.D at the School of Geospatial Engineering and Science, Sun Yat-sen University. His research interests include image and point cloud processing, semantic segmentation, 3D reconstruction, deep learning theory in 3D vision, and its applications in remote sensing and GeoAI.Weiquan Liu received the B.S. and M.S. degrees in applied mathematics from the College of Science, Jimei University, in 2013 and 2016, respectively, and the Ph.D. degree in computer science and technology from the School of Informatics, Xiamen University, in June 2020. He was a Postdoc and Associate Research Fellow with the Information and Communication Engineering Postdoctoral Research Station and the Fujian Key Laboratory of Sensing and Computing for Smart Cities, School of Informatics, Xiamen University, from August 2020 to November 2023. He is currently a Associate professor with the College of Computer Engineering, Jimei University. His current research interests include 3D vision, 3D point cloud processing, 3D adversarial learning, and remote sensing.Yu Zang received the B.S. and Ph.D. degrees from Xi’an Jiaotong University, in 2008 and 2014, respectively. He is currently a Research Associate Professor with the School of Informatics, Xiamen University. His main research interests include remote sensing image processing, computer vision and graphics, and mobile light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data analysis.Jonathan Li received the Ph.D. degree in geomatics engineering from the University of Cape Town, South Africa, in 2000. He is currently a professor of geomatics and systems design engineering with the University of Waterloo. He has supervised over 200 master’s/Ph.D. students, post-doctoral fellows and visiting scholars. He is a fellow of the Canadian Academy of Engineering, the Royal Society of Canada (Academy of Science), and the Engineering Institute of Canada, and the President of the Canadian Institute of Geomatics (CIG). His main research interests include AI-based information extraction from earth observation images and LiDAR point clouds, pointgrammetry and remote sensing, GeoAI and 3D vision for digital twin cities and autonomous driving.Cheng Wang received the Ph.D. degree in signal and information processing from the National University of Defense Technology, in 2002. He is currently a Professor with the School of Informatics, Xiamen University, and Executive Director of the Fujian Key Laboratory of Sensing and Computing for Smart Cities. His research interests cover point cloud analysis, multi-sensor fusion, mobile mapping, and geospatial big data.

item.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and environmental drivers of older pedestrian traffic crashes in Hong Kong: a spatial machine learning approach
item.dc:title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and environmental drivers of older pedestrian traffic crashes in Hong Kong: a spatial machine learning approach
item.dc:creator: Jian Liu Ketong Shen Farasath Hasan Xintao Liu Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, ChinaJian Liu is a PhD candidate in the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. His research interest focuses on urban informatics, human mobility, and accessible & inclusive cities.Ketong Shen received his PhD degree from the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. His research interest focuses on urban informatics, human perceptions, and social inequality.Farasath Hasan is a PhD candidate in the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. His research interests are urban informatics, spatial analysis, and urban growth dynamics.Xintao Liu is an Associate Professor in the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. He obtained his PhD from the Royal Institute of Technology (KTH). His research focuses on GIScience, transportation geography, and complex networks, aiming to leverage state-of-the-art technologies to advance smart cities and improve urban life, and he is particularly interested in integrating machine learning into modeling human behavior and analyzing human-environment interaction in cyber and physical spaces. He currently holds various academic leadership positions, including Chair of the Commission on Geospatial Analysis and Modeling for the International Cartographic Association (ICA), and Secretary-General of the Hong Kong GIS Association.
